section_entries.label: Scattering relations and spectral quantization
section_entries.mathematical_role: Uses the Fourier scattering map, parity-sector gamma factors, CPT action, and functional equations to state zeta/beta zero conditions and interpret nontrivial and trivial spectral points.

unit_result_entry.title: The boundary condition regularizes dilation while breaking parity degeneracy
unit_result_entry.why_material: The source interprets the local phase-space boundary as a symmetry-respecting alternative to a naive cutoff, decomposes the complete shifted Hamiltonian into partial-wave contributions, and explains that zeta/beta branches break the original even/odd degeneracy while retaining m-degeneracy.

unit_dependency_entry.context_note: The solar-mass density estimate is an illustrative physical scale, not validation of the spectral construction; the Hamiltonian decomposition depends on the earlier choice of normalization.
unit_dependency_entry.representation_dependency: The spectral sum and numerical scale are formula-sensitive. The prose-level claims about regularization, degeneracy, and density are recoverable, but exact factors need PDF verification.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Odd parity changes the spectral condition from zeta to Dirichlet beta
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: The sign carried by odd eigenfunctions modifies the equivalence relation, and the Dirichlet beta functional equation supplies the corresponding discrete odd-wave spectrum. This exposes how a representation-theoretic branch choice changes the arithmetic spectral object.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Trivial zeros are mapped to imaginary-energy resonances
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: The source distinguishes nontrivial real-energy spectral conditions from trivial zeros and interprets the latter through poles and zeros of the scattering matrix on imaginary energy axes as unstable resonances.

related_synthesis_entries.claim: Equivalent Hamiltonian normalizations can preserve the scattering matrix while the added boundary condition affects observables selectively: dilation energy becomes discrete in the proposal, whereas light-cone momentum remains continuous.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: The equivalences and observable behavior are established only for the cited near-horizon construction, not as a general principle for arbitrary Hamiltonians or boundaries.
related_synthesis_entries.title: Representation choice versus observable consequence

related_synthesis_entries.claim: Reflection parity propagates through inversion eigenvalues and scattering gamma factors so that the even branch is paired with Riemann zeta and the odd branch with Dirichlet beta, breaking their initial twofold degeneracy.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: The exact branch correspondence relies on extracted signs, powers, and gamma factors that require verification against the PDF.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The boundary regularizes by selecting a symmetry-compatible domain rather than truncating phase space; its observable mark is selective degeneracy breaking, with zeta and beta separating parity while rotational m-degeneracy survives.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The source presents the phase-space boundary as an alternative to a cutoff and says it discretizes the dilation spectrum while respecting the Hamiltonian and scattering symmetries. The full shifted Hamiltonian is decomposed into partial-wave energies: even contributions are assigned zeta zeros, odd contributions beta zeros, the original parity degeneracy is broken, and the (2l+1) m-degeneracy remains. An illustrative solar-mass estimate gives an extremely dense spectrum.
directed.conceptual_reading: A boundary condition can regularize through admissibility rather than removal of large coordinates. Comparing which degeneracies split and which persist diagnoses the symmetries the new domain breaks or preserves.
directed.representation_or_bridge: Arithmetic zero parameters supply the partial-wave dilation energies, the l-dependent Hamiltonian shift restores the complete normalization, and the asymptotic-observer dictionary translates them into physical frequency units.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The density estimate is illustrative rather than validation, the decomposition depends on the earlier Hamiltonian normalization, and discreteness does not resolve the later unbounded-below spectrum.
directed.uncertainty: The qualitative degeneracy claims are prose-grounded, but the spectral sum, numerical scale, and exact factors require PDF verification.

supported: The span describes the phase-space boundary as a symmetry-respecting regularization distinct from the cited cutoff.

It decomposes the shifted Hamiltonian into partial-wave contributions, assigns even and odd branches to zeta and beta zeros, breaks the parity degeneracy while retaining the m degeneracy, and gives an illustrative dense-spectrum scale.
The candidate correctly treats the density estimate as illustration rather than validation.
inference: Interpreting regularization as restriction of admissible states rather than coordinate truncation, and using surviving versus split degeneracies to diagnose preserved structure, are faithful local readings.
unsupported_or_imported: The boundary-or-failure field says discreteness does not resolve the later unbounded-below spectrum. The unbounded-below defect appears only in the conclusion unit and is not present in this frozen span.

section_entries.label: Conclusions, limitations, acknowledgements, and funding
section_entries.mathematical_role: Separates the proposed emission-spectrum reading from an absorption/missing-lines alternative and records unresolved physical and spectral tests.

unit_result_entry.title: The same zero relations may encode missing spectral lines rather than emitted levels
unit_result_entry.why_material: The conclusion records a materially different Connes-style interpretation: equations (16)-(17) could describe absorption gaps in a continuum rather than a discrete emission spectrum, and deciding among absorption, emission, or both requires comparison of trace formulas with zeta density of states.

unit_dependency_entry.context_note: No such comparison is performed in this source, so the alternatives remain unresolved and prevent treating the physical spectral dictionary as settled.
unit_dependency_entry.representation_dependency: Prose-grounded but refers back to the formula-sensitive equivalence relations (16)-(17) and to external trace-formula work.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: The same identification leaves light-cone momentum spectra continuous
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Applying the boundary map to Kruskal momentum eigenfunctions constrains coefficients but does not discretize momentum. This is a valuable counterpoint: the boundary condition is observable-selective rather than a universal discretizer, and the source reads that invariance as evidence for horizon smoothness.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Entropy, multiparticle observables, and the missing ground state remain open tests
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: The source identifies concrete ways the proposal could fail or be sharpened: a density/partition-function calculation must test black-hole entropy and state completeness, multiparticle observables remain unchecked, and the discrete spectrum is still unbounded below despite gauging CPT.

related_synthesis_entries.claim: The source offers a layered dictionary—nontrivial zeros as real-energy levels, trivial zeros as imaginary-energy resonances, and possibly zeros as missing continuum lines—while naming density, entropy, multiparticle, and ground-state tests that could distinguish or invalidate these readings.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: These are competing physical interpretations, not mutually verified consequences, and the proposed discriminating calculations are not carried out here.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The same zero relation admits incompatible spectral semantics: zeros may label emitted discrete levels or missing lines in a continuum, and only a trace-formula versus density-of-states comparison can decide what the construction represents.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The conclusion restates the Planckian-hyperbola CPT boundary and dilation discretization, then offers a Connes-style alternative in which equations (16)-(17) describe absent absorption lines in a continuum. It says distinguishing absorption, emission, or both requires comparison of semiclassical trace formulas with the density of states derived from zeta.
directed.conceptual_reading: An algebraic set of zeros does not determine its physical interpretation. Whether zeros count present states or excluded states depends on the observable representation and the sign or structure of the associated spectral density.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The proposed discriminator bridges boundary equivalence relations to semiclassical trace formulas and zeta density of states, translating identical arithmetic data into competing emission and absorption pictures.
directed.boundary_or_failure: No trace-formula comparison is performed, so the competing physical dictionaries remain unresolved and the discrete-level interpretation cannot be treated as settled.
directed.uncertainty: The limitation is prose-grounded; it inherits the formula uncertainty of equations (16)-(17) and depends on external Connes-style work not established in this span.

supported: The conclusion explicitly offers a Connes-style missing-lines interpretation as an alternative to the discrete-level reading.
It says a comparison of semiclassical trace formulas with zeta density of states is needed to determine whether the conditions describe absorption, emission, or both.
The candidate correctly says that comparison is not performed and the physical dictionary remains unsettled.
inference: Present-state versus absent-line semantics are a useful conceptual distinction grounded in the two interpretations named by the source.
unsupported_or_imported: The spontaneous reading calls the spectral semantics incompatible, but the source explicitly allows that the conditions may describe both absorption and emission.
The directed claim that the choice depends on the sign or structure of spectral density is a plausible diagnostic idea but is not stated in the span.
context_or_ocr_risk: The passage is prose-recoverable but inherits the formula uncertainty of equations (16)-(17) and relies on external Connes-style work.
missed_mechanism: The proposed comparison is meant to distinguish or possibly combine the interpretations, not presuppose their mutual exclusion.
revision_instructions: Replace incompatible with competing or potentially coexisting, and remove the unsupported sign-of-density mechanism. State only that the source proposes trace-formula versus density-of-states comparison to decide among absorption, emission, or both.
